label: Rousseau's general will evolved into Durkheim's collective conscience and moral solidarity
description: Émile Durkheim adopted Jean-Jacques Rousseau's insights and systematically extended them into new metaphysical, ethical, or epistemological domains.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Jean-Jacques Rousseau's perspective to Émile Durkheim's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the Enlightenment & Social Contract across history into the 19th Century Divergences.

label: Defined sociology as the empirical study of external, coercive social facts
description: Émile Durkheim formulated and introduced the concept of "Social Facts (Sui Generis)", which became a seminal contribution in structural-functionalism philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in structural-functionalism.
historicalContext: Introduced during the 19th Century Divergences as part of Émile Durkheim's canonical writings.

label: Formed the central theoretical pillar for Parsonian structural functionalism
description: Talcott Parsons adopted Émile Durkheim's insights and systematically extended them into new metaphysical, ethical, or epistemological domains.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Émile Durkheim's perspective to Talcott Parsons's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Inter-epochal reception: transmitting insights from the 19th Century Divergences across history into the 20th Century Phenomenon & Analysis.
